name: Added Lane
spec: yellow diamond with two black parallel arrows, one joining from the right without merging
meaning: A lane is added from the right; no merge needed.

snippets.back: Yellow warnings preview wet slipperiness, merging traffic, divided-highway shifts, two-way traffic, ending lanes, signals ahead, crossings, added lanes, crossroads, stop or yield ahead, curves, windings.
An Added Lane sign describes highways converging and warns that traffic from the left lane may move into the right lane.
The warning sign chart shows an added lane warning sign separately from the sign for a lane merging from the right, which tells drivers to watch for other traffic.

With a lane ends sign the ending lane must yield and merge, with a merging traffic sign you make room for vehicles joining your road, and with an added lane sign the new traffic does not need to merge at all.
An Added Lane sign means traffic from another road gets its own new lane, so no merge is needed, while a Merge sign means entering vehicles may move into your lane.
An Added Lane sign means entering traffic has its own new lane, so no merge is needed at that point.

Diamond yellow-background black-letter warning signs announce hazards, direction shifts, and nearby activity ahead and demand extra care, covering signals ahead, divided highway starts and ends, gentle curves, narrow bridges and culverts, merges, added lanes needing no merge, steep hills, clearance limits, school zones and crossings, deer and pedestrian crossings with yielding, stop signs ahead, ending right lanes, and two-way traffic with right-lane driving.
An ADDED LANE warning means joining traffic has a new lane available and does not need to merge at that point.

result.summary: Multiple snippets state added lane means new traffic gets its own lane and does not need to merge; no snippet describes the two-arrow pictogram.
